incident_spec.summary: MySQL slow log entries appear for queries that finish far below `long_query_time` because `log_queries_not_using_indexes` is enabled, so non-indexed statements are logged even when they are fast.
symptoms: The slow log contains `Query_time` values around 0.0003-0.0024 seconds, well below the configured `long_query_time = 2`.
The post shows `slow-query-log = ON` and `log-queries-not-using-indexes = ON` at the same time.
The user expected only slow queries to be logged, but the file appears to record many fast statements.
incident_spec.mechanism: When `log_queries_not_using_indexes` is ON, MySQL writes qualifying non-indexed statements to the slow log even if they are faster than `long_query_time`; the time threshold is not the only gate.

facts.evidence: The pasted slow-log lines show `Query_time` values in the sub-millisecond to low-millisecond range.
The configuration explicitly enables `log_queries_not_using_indexes`, which can populate the slow log independently of the `long_query_time` threshold.

assumptions: The pasted slow-log excerpt is representative of the problematic behavior, not a complete dump of all relevant statements.
The logged statements are non-indexed or otherwise eligible for slow-log capture under `log_queries_not_using_indexes`.
The target MySQL build supports the slow-log variables shown in the post.
unknowns: Exact query texts that produced the shown slow-log lines
Whether any of the logged statements were administrative or replication-related rather than ordinary SELECTs

feasibility.rationale: The reported behavior is reproducible with synthetic data by forcing a fast full-table scan on an unindexed predicate while `slow_query_log=ON`, `long_query_time=2`, and `log_queries_not_using_indexes=ON`. Exact production data and exact query mix are unavailable, so this is a mechanism-level reproduction rather than an exact replay.
unmatched_conditions: No original production dataset or exact SQL workload is available
The exact slow-log excerpt cannot be reproduced byte-for-byte

requirements: MySQL adapter with permission to change GLOBAL variables
Access to the configured slow-log file on the test host

validation_criteria: A fast query using an unindexed predicate is written to the slow log while `long_query_time` remains at 2 seconds.
EXPLAIN shows a full scan for the non-indexed predicate query and an indexed access path for the control query.
The observed slow-log entry is a normal MySQL slow-log record rather than a general log entry.
symptom_evidence: Slow-log output contains `Query_time` values far below 2 seconds.
The query text appears in the slow log even though it executes quickly.
mechanism_evidence: The non-indexed predicate query uses `ALL` access in EXPLAIN.
The indexed control query uses `PRIMARY` / `const` access in EXPLAIN.
Slow-log capture is triggered with `log_queries_not_using_indexes=ON` and stops after cleanup restores the original globals.

metadata.root_cause: log_queries_not_using_indexes causes fast non-indexed queries to be written to the slow log

rationale: The post is best explained by MySQL's slow-log behavior when `log_queries_not_using_indexes` is enabled: a query can be fast enough to beat `long_query_time` yet still be logged if it does not use an index. The synthetic dataset creates a predictable non-indexed predicate (`category = 'cold'`) that forces a full scan, while a primary-key lookup provides an indexed control. This isolates the mechanism without needing the original production data.
